canonical_statement: The study compared the safety and efficacy of total-body-weight-based versus adjusted-body-weight-based unfractionated heparin protocols in older adults and/or higher-weight adults with suspected or confirmed venous thromboembolism.
The investigation was a single-center retrospective pre-post cohort study at Cooper University Hospital.

Eligible patients were adults with suspected or confirmed venous thromboembolism who received protocolized unfractionated heparin for at least 24 hours and were age 65 years or older and/or weighed at least 100 kg.

population.label: Adults with suspected or confirmed VTE meeting age >=65 years and/or weight >=100 kg criteria
inclusion_criteria: At least one anti-Xa level after heparin initiation
UFH protocol for at least 24 hours

canonical_statement: Patients were excluded for significant protocol variation, pregnancy, incarceration, oral factor-Xa inhibitor exposure during or directly before the index admission, ECMO during UFH infusion, missing height, or height 152.4 cm or less.

population.label: Study eligibility exclusions
exclusion_criteria: Significant variation from institutional UFH protocol
Oral factor Xa inhibitor during or directly prior to index admission before UFH

canonical_statement: Anti-Xa was targeted to 0.3-0.7 units/mL, checked approximately 6 hours after initiation and rate changes until two consecutive therapeutic levels, then every 24 hours while therapeutic.
The total-body-weight cohort was screened from July 1 through September 30, 2019, and the adjusted-body-weight cohort from July 1 through September 30, 2021.
The primary endpoint was time from UFH initiation to the first therapeutic anti-Xa level, with therapeutic anti-Xa defined as 0.3-0.7 units/mL.

concept.text: Time to first therapeutic anti-Xa level

outcome.definition: Time from UFH initiation to first anti-Xa 0.3-0.7 units/mL

canonical_statement: Secondary endpoints included the proportion of first measured anti-Xa values in range and the proportion of therapeutic anti-Xa measurements during the first 24 hours of UFH.

concept.text: Therapeutic anti-Xa measurements

outcome.definition: First anti-Xa in range and therapeutic anti-Xa values in first 24 hours

canonical_statement: Safety endpoints were in-hospital mortality and ISTH major bleeding.

concept.text: ISTH major bleeding and in-hospital mortality

outcome.definition: Major bleeding: overt bleeding with hemoglobin decrease >=2 g/dL, transfusion of >=2 units, critical-site bleeding, or bleeding contributing to death

canonical_statement: The primary endpoint was analyzed with the Mann-Whitney U test and Hodges-Lehmann estimator; secondary endpoints used Pearson chi-square or Fisher exact tests, with prespecified age/weight subgroups and a post-hoc bolus subgroup.
Of 571 screened patients, 90 met eligibility criteria; 10 were randomly excluded to balance strata, leaving 80 patients, 40 in each cohort.
Each cohort contained 27 patients age 65 years or older and under 100 kg, 11 patients under age 65 years and at least 100 kg, and 2 patients meeting both age and weight criteria.
Concomitant antithrombotic medication use at baseline was more frequent in the adjusted-body-weight cohort than the total-body-weight cohort (85% vs 62.5%; p=0.02).

canonical_statement: The authors identified the retrospective, single-center design and institution-specific UFH monitoring/titration protocol as limitations to generalizability.
Anti-Xa samples collected later than six hours after initiation or a rate change and hemolyzed samples requiring redraws could have prolonged measured time to therapeutic anti-Xa.
The primary endpoint was a laboratory endpoint rather than patient-centered efficacy or safety outcomes such as successful VTE treatment or reduced bleeding.

Excluding 44 patients who had received oral factor-Xa inhibitors during or directly before the index admission limits applicability to patients transitioning from agents such as apixaban or rivaroxaban.
The higher-weight-only subgroup included only 11 patients per cohort and was likely underpowered to detect a difference in time to therapeutic anti-Xa.

The authors concluded that adjusted-body-weight UFH dosing shortened time to therapeutic anti-Xa in the combined older/higher-weight population, with the observed effect driven primarily by older adults and no statistically significant benefit shown in higher-weight patients under age 65.
The authors called for a larger prospective randomized trial to determine whether adjusted-body-weight UFH improves clinical efficacy and minimizes bleeding compared with total-body-weight dosing.
The authors reported receiving no support from any organization for the submitted work.
The authors reported no relevant financial or non-financial interests to disclose.
Study data are not publicly available because of participant privacy; de-identified data may be requested from the corresponding author subject to IRB approval and data-use requirements.

The main article refers to Online Resource 1 for the UFH titration protocol and Online Resource 2 for major bleeding event details; those supplementary resources are not embedded in the retrieved seven-page PDF.
